verified.exploit_entry_point: The i18next backend module's public methods: read(language, namespace, cb), readMulti(languages, namespaces, cb) and create(languages, namespace, key, value, cb). Each builds a request URL from the configured location template and the supplied values and hands it to the selected transport. Hidden tests drive those methods against local HTTP servers (fetch and the legacy XMLHttpRequest polyfill) and assert on what the servers receive.
sites: lib/index.js:74 (loadUrl hands the built URL to the configured transport)
lib/request.js:89-97 (fetch request options: the transport follows a redirect by default)
lib/request.js:162-170 (transport selection: fetch unless file:, otherwise XMLHttpRequest)
routes: T1: read, readMulti and both configured-location forms (string, function, promise) with a value that supplies a scheme, a path escape, a namespace escape, a query injection or a joined multi-value escape; also through the legacy XMLHttpRequest transport
T2: the opt-in write path (create/addPath) with the same value forms
T7: a redirect served by the configured destination, for a read and for a write

T8: the value rule must stay scoped: relative default and leading-placeholder locations, the falsy-location abort, query string parameters, the + join, regional language tags, and the verbatim URL contract of an app-supplied request handler
verified.project_tests_run: node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/http.spec.js test/request.spec.js test/backendConnector.load.spec.js, run once on the default fetch transport and once with --require test/fixtures/xmlHttpRequest.cjs (pinned, reference, alternative, hardening and every check patch)

traps.pattern: A (advisory route; the read-side URL guard)
traps.shape: a caller-supplied language or namespace value becomes part of the request destination: a scheme delimiter where the template starts with the placeholder, traversal out of the configured path, a query injection, or an escape introduced by joining several values; reached through a string, function or promise location and through both transports
traps.realistic_because: the reported route and the site both published fixes touch; the value rule is a denylist in 3.0.5 that missed the scheme delimiter closed in 4.0.2

traps.pattern: A (far site; the second request sink)
traps.shape: the same supplied-value URL construction on the opt-in write path (create/addPath), which the reported read route never touches
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the write endpoint is dormant unless the application enables saveMissing and configures addPath; it reads as an opt-in feature the application owns, while the report is about fetching translations
traps.realistic_because: the published fixes change create() as well as _readAny(); a fix aimed at the reported read route leaves this sink open

traps.pattern: B (uncovered route; the protection never existed at the transport)
traps.shape: a response from the configured destination redirects the request to another destination; the transport follows it, so a request is delivered somewhere the application did not configure
traps.reason_to_dismiss: following redirects is normal HTTP, the configured destination is trusted, and refusing them would break CDN canonicalisation; no published fix touches the transport
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both published fixes validate the constructed value and leave the transport's redirect behaviour untouched, and current upstream still does

traps.shape: a rule that is scoped to the supplied values keeps every documented shape working: a relative default, a template that starts with the placeholder, the falsy-location abort, query string parameters, the + join, regional language tags and the verbatim URL handed to an app-supplied request handler; an absolute-http(s)-only rule or a rewriting rule breaks them
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the visible values are the legitimate ones, so an absolute-http(s)-only rule looks like the safe reading of the report
traps.realistic_because: the project documents the relative default, the falsy-location abort, query parameters and a custom request handler; MIMO-class over-hardening is the failure mode

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protection is a library value check, not a server response; a thrown exception reaches the caller as a failed read and the project's own tests fail, so it cannot score 1.0
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the only transformation between a supplied value and the request is interpolation, and the reference validates the value itself; there is no normalising step that turns a checked value into a different bad one
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: values reach interpolation as plain strings joined by '+'; there is no alternate spelling that the matcher and the URL parser read differently without an encoding variant
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the destination comes from the application's configured template; there is no external authority that can return no decision

advisories.scope: 3.0.5: interpolated language/namespace values validated against a denylist on reads and writes
4.0.2: the denylist also rejects the scheme delimiter in both values and a namespace carrying '//'
